findings.body:
If `PROCESSOR_KEY` is set, this `log.debug` call puts the live payment-processor credential into the structured log payload. Debug logs are typically shipped to the same aggregators, support consoles, and CI artifacts as info logs, so anyone who can read those streams can extract the key and replay charges.

Log `orderId` and `ref` only. Keep the processor key in env/secret storage and out of log fields.

summary:
Looks good except for a critical secret leak: `charge()` now writes `process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY` into the debug log payload, so the payment-processor credential can land in log aggregators, support tools, and CI artifacts. Restore the previous non-secret charge log and keep the key out of any structured payload.

The comment on the same hunk states the intent is to include credentials so support can replay failures. That is the failure mode, not a justification: anyone with log access can extract the processor key and replay charges. Debug level does not contain this; most production pipelines still ship debug logs.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head code at src/payments/charge.ts:7 explicitly logs process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY in the structured debug payload; the patch replaced a safe orderId/ref info log with this credential leak. That supports a critical secret-exposure finding.
